# Author writing sample (published paper, excerpt) — match this voice

Coral reefs are not dying everywhere at once. They are dying in patches — and the patches matter.

We surveyed 112 reef sites across three archipelagos. At each site we counted live coral cover along
three 50-m transects. The pattern was blunt: cover fell where summer anomalies exceeded 1 °C for more
than four weeks, and held where they did not. We think the threshold is real. We are less sure it is
universal — our sites share a single ocean basin.

Two caveats deserve space. First, transects undercount cryptic species. Second — and more important —
we sampled once per site, so we cannot separate a slow decline from a single bleaching event.
